claims.claim: **Diagnosis is the triad:** heavy proteinuria (dipstick over 3+ or spot protein/creatinine ratio over 200 mg/mmol), hypoalbuminaemia (albumin under 25 g/L) and oedema.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Remission** = urine protein negative or trace on 3 days running. **Relapse** = proteinuria over 3+ on 3 days running — mild illness is a frequent trigger.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most children respond to prednisolone and do not need a renal biopsy**; about 85% of steroid-sensitive children relapse at least once and 50% relapse frequently.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weigh the child and compare with pre-illness weight** — weight gain may be the only sign of fluid overload. Measure BP against age and gender ranges and confirm manually.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Intravascular volume depletion:** abdominal cramps · dizziness · tachycardia · poor perfusion · reduced urine output · transient hypertension · hypotension · shock.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Infection:** encapsulated bacteria (complement loss). **Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis** presents with abdominal pain with rebound, fever and vomiting — **signs can be masked by steroids.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Thrombosis** can be venous or arterial, at any site — e.g. central venous, renal vein, pulmonary embolism.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Atypical features — discuss with Nephrology early:** age under 1 or over 12 years · nephritic features · persistent hypertension or renal impairment · significant complications at first presentation · features of systemic disease · dysmorphism.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Standard:** urine dipstick, urine MCS, spot protein/creatinine ratio, UEC, LFTs, albumin, FBE. **Complement, ANA/ANCA and anti-streptococcal antibodies** only if creatinine is raised, the history is atypical or systemic disease is suspected.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blood culture if febrile or systemically unwell**; chest X-ray if effusion or pulmonary oedema is suspected; renal ultrasound with Doppler for unclear diagnosis, significant flank/abdominal pain, atypical history or poor diuretic response.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Admit all children on their first presentation.** Strict fluid balance, urine output in mL/kg/hr, daily weights on the same scales at the same time.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sodium restriction: 2–3 mmol/kg** (about 40 mg/kg or 2 g/day); a low or no-added-salt diet is usually enough.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fluid restriction to 50–70% of maintenance over 24 hours**, particularly if Na under 130 mmol/L; **do not count albumin in the allowance.** Mild hyponatraemia often corrects with fluid restriction alone.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **20% albumin 5 mL/kg (1 g/kg) over 4 hours** for intravascular depletion and/or severe or symptomatic oedema. **Consider IV furosemide 0.5–1 mg/kg (max 40 mg)** at the middle and/or end of the infusion.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Monitor closely for hypertension and pulmonary oedema during albumin; run infusions in the day with adequate staffing.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Use diuretics cautiously, usually only with albumin** — they can precipitate intravascular depletion, AKI and thrombosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First presentation: prednisolone 60 mg/m² or 2 mg/kg (max 60 mg) orally daily for 4 weeks**, however quickly remission comes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Relapse: prednisolone 60 mg/m² or 2 mg/kg (max 60 mg) orally daily only until remission.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Followed by prednisolone 40 mg/m² or 1.5 mg/kg (max 40 mg) orally on alternate days for 4 weeks, then stop.** A relapse during this period goes back to 60 mg/m² or 2 mg/kg (max 60 mg) daily until remission, then repeats the step-down.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If oral intake is not tolerated, give IV methylprednisolone at 80% of the oral prednisolone dose.** Round prednisolone up to the easiest dose; tablets can be crushed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Steroid-dependent NS** = two relapses in a row while the prednisolone dose is being reduced, or a relapse within 15 days after it is stopped.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Antibiotics are not indicated unless there is pneumococcal risk** (e.g. gross oedema, unimmunised). **No routine acid suppression** unless upper GI symptoms on steroids.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Additional meningococcal and pneumococcal vaccines and yearly influenza vaccine.** ⚠️ **Delay live vaccines until 1 month off steroids.** Consider varicella immunoglobulin after chickenpox exposure in an unimmunised child in relapse or on steroids.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **VTE prophylaxis:** above-knee TED stockings are usually all that is needed for mobile children over 12 years without other VTE risk factors.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Adrenal suppression risk after stopping steroids:** consider adrenal stimulation testing if cushingoid or frequently relapsing.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve paediatric nephrology** for atypical features, significant complications, **proteinuria persisting after 4 weeks of prednisolone**, refractory oedema, or steroid toxicity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** oedema is manageable without regular IV albumin and weight is not rising, steroids have started, and education and follow-up are done.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Home dipstick daily (first-morning urine) until proteinuria resolves, then twice a week or more through the first year**; back to daily if 1+ or more protein, intercurrent infection, oedema or suspected relapse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tell families about adrenal suppression** and give written information on possible steroid need in acute illness or trauma.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Nephrotic syndrome' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Nephrotic_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23
